provenance.note: Re-runs the sq-jaj38 (http-protocol) and sq-1uuxz (federation-descriptors) served-surface lanes in-process against the sparq-server loopback endpoint. Pass/divergence/fail counts are conformance facts; `floor` is each suite's ratchet floor (may only rise) from crates/sparq-conformance/src/scoreboard.rs. Documented divergences are reported per-assertion and are NEVER summed into `pass`, so a documented gap can never inflate the conformance number.
provenance.run_source: https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions (per-build artifact); authoritative per-release reports attach to each GitHub Release

suites.label: W3C SPARQL 1.1 Protocol (HTTP)
suites.note: SPARQL 1.1 Protocol operations (GET/POST query+update, the QUERY method, dataset overrides, SRJ/SRX/CSV/TSV negotiation, 200/400/405/406/415) over RAW HTTP against the in-process loopback server; a present-but-unsatisfiable Accept now returns 406 (Oxigraph parity, sq-406acc); the absent/*/* Accept JSON default + ASK-in-CSV are documented divergences, NOT summed into the floor

tests.label: query via GET (?query=…) → 200 + SRJ, 1 default-graph row
query via POST urlencoded (query= body) → 200 + SRJ
query via POST direct (application/sparql-query) → 200 + SRJ
query via the HTTP QUERY method (application/sparql-query) → 200 + SRJ
QUERY method rejects application/sparql-update body → 415
QUERY method rejects update= form field → 400
SELECT Accept application/sparql-results+json → 200 + SRJ
SELECT Accept application/sparql-results+xml → 200 + SRX
SELECT Accept text/csv → 200 + text/csv
SELECT Accept text/tab-separated-values → 200 + TSV
ASK Accept application/sparql-results+json → 200 + SRJ boolean true
ASK Accept application/sparql-results+xml → 200 + SRX
default-graph-uri=g1 re-scopes the default graph → 1 row (g1's triple)
named-graph-uri=g1 exposes exactly g1 as a named graph → 1 row
update via POST (application/sparql-update INSERT DATA) → 2xx
POST update genuinely mutated the store (ASK new triple → true)
GET /sparql with no query parameter → 400
GET /sparql with a malformed query → 400
POST /sparql with an unsupported Content-Type (text/plain) → 415
DELETE /sparql → 405 with an Allow header
unsatisfiable Accept (image/png) on SELECT → 406 Not Acceptable (Oxigraph parity, sq-406acc)

tests.detail: absent / */* Accept defaults to SPARQL-results JSON (W3C-permitted default representation); only a present-but-unsatisfiable Accept is 406
tests.label: absent / */* Accept on SELECT still defaults to SRJ, not 406 (sq-406acc)

tests.detail: CSV/TSV have no SPARQL boolean serialisation, so an ASK with Accept: text/csv falls back to a JSON boolean (ask_content_type)
tests.label: ASK Accept text/csv falls back to a JSON boolean (CSV has no boolean form)

suites.label: SPARQL 1.1 Service Description + Graph Store Protocol
suites.note: the GET /sparql (no query) Service-Description advertises exactly the formats/languages/versions/features the server genuinely implements (no over-advertising), PLUS a GET/PUT/POST/DELETE Graph-Store-Protocol round-trip (named + default graph, indirect + direct identification) verifying store state after each op; absent-graph 200-empty read is a documented divergence, NOT summed in

tests.label: Service Description: GET /sparql (no query) → 200 + N-Triples
SD types an sd:Service with an sd:endpoint
SD advertises sd:SPARQL11Query + the version-agnostic sd:SPARQLQuery
SD advertises sd:SPARQL11Update + sd:SPARQLUpdate (anonymous Update possible, no write-token)
advertised sd:SPARQL11Update is genuine (anonymous POST update succeeds → 2xx)
SD advertises sd:supportedVersion 1.0 / 1.1 / 1.2
SD advertises full version-1.2, NOT the -basic profile
SD advertises sd:resultFormat for SRJ / SRX / CSV / TSV (solution sets)
SD advertises sd:resultFormat for Turtle / N-Triples / RDF-XML (graphs)
SD advertises sd:inputFormat for Turtle / N-Triples / RDF-XML
SD advertises sd:BasicFederatedQuery (the SERVICE clause is genuinely compiled in)
SD does NOT over-advertise JSON-LD (sparq-server/jsonld is not on in this build)
advertised sd:resultFormat SRJ is genuinely served (SELECT Accept → that media type)
advertised sd:resultFormat SRX is genuinely served (SELECT Accept → that media type)
advertised sd:resultFormat CSV is genuinely served (SELECT Accept → that media type)
advertised sd:resultFormat TSV is genuinely served (SELECT Accept → that media type)
GSP PUT new named graph (indirect ?graph=) → 201 Created
GSP GET the PUT graph returns it equal (PUT→GET round-trip)
GSP PUT existing named graph REPLACES → 204 No Content
GSP PUT replaced the graph (old triple gone, new present)
GSP POST to existing named graph MERGES → 204
GSP POST merged additively (both s2 and s3 present)
GSP DELETE named graph → 204 No Content
GSP DELETE removed the graph (GET returns empty)
GSP DELETE an absent named graph → 404 Not Found

tests.detail: sparq serialises an absent graph as the empty graph (200, empty body) on a GSP read; it does not 404 (the GSP spec permits treating an empty graph as existing)
tests.label: GSP GET an absent named graph is 200 + empty graph, not 404 (GSP-permitted empty-graph read)
GSP PUT new graph (direct /graphs/<path>) → 201 Created
GSP GET the direct-form graph returns it equal
GSP DELETE via indirect ?graph= naming the direct IRI → 204 (forms address one graph)
GSP direct + indirect identification address the SAME graph (GET now empty)
GSP PUT default graph (?default) → 2xx
GSP PUT default graph replaced it (new triple present, fixture triple gone)
GSP POST default graph (?default) MERGES → 204
GSP POST default graph merged (both default triples present)
GSP DELETE default graph (?default) → 204 (empties it)
GSP DELETE default graph emptied it (GET returns empty)
GSP PUT with a malformed RDF body → 400
GSP PUT with an unsupported Content-Type (image/png) → 415
GSP GET /sparql/graph with no graph selector → 400
GSP unsupported verb (TRACE) → 405 with an Allow header
